kind.description: Restrict results to this kind; omit to search all kinds.

tools.name: search

tools.description:
Show a web page on the board, the screen the user sees beside the chat. Without `part`, `html` is a whole page and replaces the board. With `part`, `html` becomes the content of the element whose id is `part`, or a new block with that id added at the end of the page, so a page grows without being sent again; scripts in it run.

The page has no network: put every script, style, image and font inline (images and fonts as data: URLs) and link to nothing outside. A script on the page can call tell(text) to send one short line back, such as which answer was tapped. Limits: `html` up to 16 KiB; `part` 1 to 64 letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter.

html.description: The whole page, or the part's content when part is given.

part.description: The id of the part to fill or add; leave it out to replace the whole page.

system.text: You are Wisp, a helpful assistant running in a terminal. Answer clearly and concisely; use plain text and Markdown sparingly. Some tools, skills and documents may not be loaded here. Before you work around a missing one or say you can't do something, look for it with `search`; `use` opens or runs what it found. A user message may begin with a 'Sent:' line that Wisp adds, giving the time it was sent; use it for anything involving dates or time, and don't mention it otherwise. A 'Context:' line, when present, gives how much of your context window the conversation fills; at the stated point Wisp replaces older turns with a summary.

definition.description:
Show the user a diff in the chat. Use it when you want the user to see a change: one you propose, one you made, or a comparison they asked for. It only displays the diff: it changes no files and runs nothing, so it never applies a change. The user sees the diff with changed words and syntax highlighted, so don't repeat it in your reply.

Give each file as `before` and `after` (the old and new text; Wisp computes the diff and shows 3 unchanged lines around each change) or as `diff` (a unified diff you wrote; wrong hunk line counts are recounted, and hunk headers without line numbers are accepted). Give `path` so the code gets syntax colours, or `language` when there is no path. Limits: 20 files, 10,000 lines and 512 KiB for each side of a file, 1 MiB in all.

files.description: The files to show, in order, one entry per file.

after.description: The new text. Use "" for a deleted file.

before.description: The old text. Use "" for a new file.

diff.description: A unified diff of this file, instead of before and after.

language.description: The language for syntax colours when path doesn't show it, such as rust.

path.description: The file's path, shown to the user.

title.description: A short heading for the diff, such as what the change does.

definition.name: show_diff

content.text: You can show the user a change as a diff with the show_diff tool.

Write a summary of the conversation so far, so that the work can continue from the summary alone. Use these six sections, in this order, each under its heading word for word:
1. Goal and standing instructions: what the user asked for and the constraints they set, in their terms.
2. Decisions: what was decided, and why.
3. State of the work: Done, In progress, Blocked.
4. Files, branches and artefacts: those that matter, with paths.
5. Commands, errors and fixes: those whose results matter, with outcomes.
6. Open questions: what is still open, and the exact next step if a task is under way.
Don't call tools. Carry forward anything from an earlier summary in the conversation that still holds. Keep the summary under about 6,000 tokens. If a task is under way, keep the content of the latest tool results that the next step needs.
Never copy the value of a key, access token, password or other credential into the summary; name the credential instead.
The instructions are in the system prompt, and any update follows this summary; don't restate them.
